articles.title: Tesla Sets October 1 Launch Date for Long-Delayed Roadster
articles.sourceName: Brand Icon Image - Latest Brand, Tech And Business
articles.description: Electric-car maker signals return of its high-performance sports car nearly a decade after unveiling next-generation model. Tesla has set October 1 as the date for a highly anticipated launch event for its next-generation Roadster, reviving a programme that has been repeatedly delayed since the electric-vehicle maker first unveiled the sports car nearly a decade ago. The company signalled the date on Saturday through its website and social media accounts, posting “Go for launch” on X alongside a graphic displaying the date “10.01.” The announcement has renewed attention around Tesla’s long-awaited Roadster, which was first introduced in 2017 with promises that deliveries would begin in 2020. Those plans have since been pushed back several times, leaving the vehicle in development far longer than originally anticipated. The Roadster is expected to occupy a distinctive place in Tesla’s lineup as a high-performance, two-seat electric sports car designed to showcase the company’s technology and performance capabilities. Possible SpaceX-linked demonstration The October event could also feature a demonstration of a limited-edition Roadster fitted with cold-gas thrusters developed in collaboration with SpaceX, according to a report by The Information in August. The report said the demonstration could take place at SpaceX’s test facility in McGregor, Texas. The proposed technology has attracted particular interest because of Tesla CEO Elon Musk’s previous claims that the thruster-equipped Roadster could deliver performance capabilities beyond those of conventional electric sports cars. Tesla has not publicly confirmed all of the details surrounding the reported demonstration. The Roadster programme dates back to Tesla’s early years. The company’s original Roadster, launched in 2008, was its first production vehicle and helped establish Tesla as a serious player in the emerging electric-vehicle industry. The second-generation model was presented in 2017 as a much more powerful successor, but its production timeline has repeatedly slipped. Roadster launch comes amid robotaxi push The renewed focus on the Roadster comes as Tesla accelerates efforts in another major area of its business: autonomous driving. Last week, the company began offering rides in its two-seat Cybercab in limited areas of Austin, Texas. The vehicle is designed without a conventional steering wheel or pedals, reflecting Tesla’s ambitions to develop fully autonomous transportation. Musk has described the Cybercab as central to his vision of transforming Tesla into a dominant force in driverless vehicles. The simultaneous development of the Roadster and Cybercab highlights the breadth of Tesla’s current product ambitions. While the Roadster is aimed at performance and technology enthusiasts, the Cybercab is being positioned as part of a potentially much larger autonomous-transportation business. For Tesla, the October 1 event could therefore serve as more than a long-awaited product unveiling. It may also provide the company with an opportunity to demonstrate how far its vehicle technology has advanced since the Roadster was first announced in 2017. After years of delays, investors and Tesla enthusiasts will be watching closely to see whether the October event finally marks the beginning of the Roadster’s journey into production—or another milestone in an unusually prolonged development programme.
